scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2,
PC5 at 10.5.0.5) say they cannot reach anything outside their
own subnet. They can still ping each other. Campus 2 VLAN 6
users (PC3, PC4) are unaffected and have full connectivity.
Identify the fault.

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v5 SVI (10.5.0.254/24)
Mechanism: sshswitch is the multilayer switch that provides
  L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200. PCs in
  VLAN 5 (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) use 10.5.0.254 as their default
  gateway. When the br_v5 bridge interface goes down, the
  SVI IP becomes unreachable; packets from PCs to off-subnet
  destinations have no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
  unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v5 bridge interface is administratively down
  on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The default gateway SVI for Campus 2 VLAN 5 on sshswitch (bridge interface br_v5, IP 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively down.

Mechanism: VLAN 5 hosts (10.5.0.0/24) can exchange traffic at Layer 2 and ping each other, but their default gateway 10.5.0.254 is unreachable. With the SVI down, ARP for the gateway fails and no L3 forwarding occurs, so they cannot reach any external subnets. Meanwhile, VLAN 6’s SVI (br_v6, 10.6.0.254) is up and routing normally, explaining why VLAN 6 users have full connectivity.

Localization: On sshswitch, ip_addr shows br_v5 is in “state DOWN” with no UP flag, while br_v6 and the trunk subinterface bond0.6 are UP and carrying traffic. Switch4’s VLAN 5 ports/bridge are UP, so the issue is not on the access switch. Router17’s routing table includes 10.6.0.0/24 via 55.5.1.2 (sshswitch) but not 10.5.0.0/24, consistent with br_v5 being down and not advertised.

Root cause: The VLAN 5 SVI (br_v5) on sshswitch was left administratively down.

Corrective fix: Bring the gateway interface up on sshswitch and ensure it persists across reboots: ip link set br_v5 up. Verify bond0.5 remains a member of br_v5 and that OSPF on sshswitch advertises 10.5.0.0/24 again. After bringing up br_v5, VLAN 5 hosts should ARP and route externally, and remote routers will learn 10.5.0.0/24, restoring full connectivity.
